papers.title: Strength of evidence for paternal influence on offspring epigenome in observational human studies: a systematic review and risk-of-bias appraisal for non-randomized exposures.
papers.one_line: A systematic review of 28 observational studies of paternal exposures and the offspring epigenome rated every one at high (18) or very high (10) risk of bias under ROBINS-E, with confounding (mean domain score 2.91) and exposure measurement (2.68) the worst domains, and proposed target trial emulation as the remedy.
papers.what_was_done: Three databases were searched for human studies published between 2003 and 2023 assessing paternal factors before or during pregnancy against epigenetic outcomes, yielding 28 studies concentrated on paternal BMI or obesity (7), age (7), smoking (5) and socioeconomic status (4). All 28 measured DNA methylation and two additionally measured miRNA expression; 21 of 28 measured the outcome at delivery in cord blood. Risk of bias was scored on the seven ROBINS-E domains with bespoke decision rules written for this question, including a three-part test of whether the exposure was well defined. Every study was rated high (18) or very high (10) overall; six were auto-assigned very high because confounding was not considered at all, leaving only 22 studies with domain-specific ratings. Mean domain scores on a one-to-four scale were 2.91 for confounding, 2.68 for exposure measurement, 2.18 for missing data and 2.18 for selection of participants. Across studies there was little to no overlap in the CpG sites or genomic regions reported, except that smoking and paternal education showed a consistent absence of association. Exposures that were stable over the window, such as socioeconomic status and age, scored better on exposure measurement than behavioral exposures whose timing and dose were unspecified.

future_research.gap: Population and exposure definitions have to be specified before the field can produce replicable estimates, and target trial emulation is proposed as the vehicle
future_research.quote: Aligning study design more closely with clinical trials or animal models, by clearly defining populations and exposures, may result in more reliable and replicable findings.

problems.evidence: Paternal BMI was the most studied exposure across seven studies and produced no overlapping CpG sites, which is attributed to the exposure label spanning physiologically distinct states: over-nutrition, under-nutrition, exercise, weight training, pharmacology and metabolic pathophysiology all land in the same category. No procedure in the review or in the studies it appraises defines which of those states belong in one treatment version and which do not.
problems.quote: Consequently, individuals with similar high (or low) BMI may have different underlying physiology with corresponding differential impacts on paternal physiology, sperm epigenomics, and fetal programming.

problems.evidence: Target trial emulation is recommended for exposures that are attributes rather than interventions: paternal BMI, age, socioeconomic status and education. None of these has a stated assignment unit, an intervention that could be delivered, or a set of treatment versions, and the review's own finding is that the exposures with the least defined experimental analogue produced the least reproducible results. The recommendation therefore transfers the framework to a class of questions where its protocol components cannot be filled in.
problems.quote: Frameworks like ‘target trial emulation,’ offer a promising approach to improve reproducibility and interpretability of future research on paternal effects on offspring epigenome.

problems.evidence: All 28 studies were rated high or very high risk of bias and all 28 remain in the synthesis; the rating changes how findings are discussed but stops nothing. Six studies were assigned the worst overall rating for not considering confounding at all and were still carried through the results. A rating scale without a threshold that removes a study is a narrative judgment attached to an already published estimate.
problems.quote: All studies included in the review were rated ‘high’ (18 studies) or ‘very high’ (10 studies) for the overall Risk of Bias

problems.evidence: ROBINS-E is applied as a seven-domain profile, which is closer to an assumption dashboard than a single quality label and does separate confounding from missing data and from participant selection. What it does not do is distinguish diagnosable from undiagnosable: the domains collapse into one overall rating, six studies received the overall rating with no domain scores at all, and the confounding score of 2.91 sits on the same one-to-four scale as the missing data score of 2.18 despite one being checkable against the data and the other not.
problems.quote: we evaluated the quality of the studies across seven domains: confounding, exposure measurement, selection of participants, post-exposure intervention, missing data, selection of results, and outcome measurement

problems.evidence: A three-part outcome-blind rubric for exposure timing is supplied: measurement timing must align with the relevant exposure window, the measure must be a valid proxy, and dose or duration must be specified. It scores studies after the fact and it is what separates smoking studies rated high from the one rated some concerns. It does not tell an investigator how to choose the window or the permissible lag before the outcome is looked at, and no threshold on the resulting score changes any study decision.
problems.quote: In the exposure measurement domain, we established three criteria to determine whether an exposure was well-defined

problems.evidence: Paternal smoking, one of the four most studied exposures, is usually recorded by asking the mother about her partner rather than the father, and the exposure then enters analysis as a binary variable with no error model. The review scores this under exposure measurement at a mean of 2.68 out of four, but no included study propagates the misclassification into its effect estimate, so the reported absence of association between paternal smoking and offspring methylation is not distinguishable from attenuation by proxy report.
problems.quote: Most studies relied on maternal reports about paternal smoking during pregnancy

papers.title: Site-specific complications of central venous catheterization under systematic ultrasound guidance: a target trial emulation revisiting the 3SITES study.
papers.one_line: A post hoc emulation of the 3SITES randomized trial estimated catheter complication rates across three insertion sites under a counterfactual of universal real-time ultrasound guidance, although only 50 of 989 subclavian catheters (5.1%) were actually ultrasound-guided.
papers.what_was_done: The 3SITES randomized trial data from 10 French intensive care units contributed 3,409 catheters in 2,989 patients, of which 1,153 were femoral, 1,267 internal jugular and 989 subclavian. Real-time ultrasound guidance was left to clinician discretion in the original trial and was used for 967 catheters (28.4%): 196 femoral (17.0%), 721 internal jugular (56.9%) and 50 subclavian (5.1%). The emulation estimated what complication rates would have been had every catheter been placed under real-time ultrasound guidance, using stabilized inverse probability weights formed from the product of a catheter-site propensity model and an ultrasound-guidance propensity model for each of three pairwise comparisons. The primary outcome was time to catheter-related bloodstream infection or symptomatic deep-vein thrombosis; asymptomatic deep-vein thrombosis was ascertained only among patients who underwent post-removal compression ultrasonography. Weighted log-rank tests gave P = 0.02 for subclavian versus femoral and P = 0.001 for subclavian versus internal jugular on the primary composite, with no significant difference for internal jugular versus femoral (P = 0.97). Hazard ratios were not estimable in some comparisons because no events occurred in the subclavian group. Covariate balance was reported as standardized mean differences, with age and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease remaining between 0.2 and 0.3 in comparisons involving subclavian access. Missing continuous covariates were handled by regression-based single imputation and missing categorical covariates by a missing category.

future_research.gap: Operator skill determines whether ultrasound guidance delivers its benefit, and no training or credentialing procedure supports the counterfactual that all operators achieve it
future_research.quote: By addressing the training gap explicitly, future work can move beyond showing what's possible to ensuring that it becomes standard practice in ICUs globally.

problems.evidence: The counterfactual sets ultrasound guidance to one for every catheter while only 5.1% of subclavian catheters (50 of 989) were placed that way, so the subclavian arm of the intervened population is supported by fifty procedures. What is reported is covariate balance, standardized mean differences below 0.2 with age and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease between 0.2 and 0.3, which describes the weights rather than naming which operator, patient and site histories carry no ultrasound-guided subclavian data at all.
problems.quote: Of these, 967 (28.4%) were real-time ultrasound-guided: 196 (17.0%) in the femoral, 721 (56.9%) in the internal jugular, and 50 (5.1%) in the subclavian site.

problems.evidence: A trial dataset of 3,409 catheters collapses to a subclavian ultrasound-guided stratum of 50 procedures once the joint intervention is imposed, and the shortage propagates into the adjustment itself: the number of confounding factors in the models was cut to avoid quasi-complete separation. Zero events in the subclavian group left the hazard ratio undefined, and the null result for mechanical complications is acknowledged as possibly underpowered.
problems.quote: the relatively low proportion of real-time ultrasound-guided subclavian catheterization reduced the number of catheters and events in this group

problems.evidence: Real-time ultrasound guidance is treated as one binary treatment version, yet the operator taxonomy in the source trial distinguishes a resident with fewer than 50 catheterizations at that site, a senior with 50 or more, and an ultrasound guidance expert senior, and the effect is stated to depend on which of these performs the procedure. A counterfactual that sets guidance to one for the 939 subclavian catheters placed without it does not say which version of guidance those catheters would have received.
problems.quote: the benefits of ultrasound guidance are highly operator-dependent

problems.evidence: Asymptomatic deep-vein thrombosis is defined over the subset who underwent post-removal compression ultrasonography rather than over the randomized population, so the reported asymptomatic thrombosis contrast (weighted log-rank P = 0.004 subclavian versus femoral) is a data-defined estimand fixed by who happened to be available for scanning, not a noisy measurement of the intended one. Sensitivity of compression ultrasonography at the subclavian site is separately acknowledged as lower, which shifts the estimand again by site.
problems.quote: asymptomatic deep-vein thrombosis (among patients who underwent ultrasonography examination)

problems.evidence: The declared estimand is a counterfactual complication risk under universal ultrasound guidance, but the reported quantities are weighted log-rank P values plus hazard ratios where estimable, and the effect measure switches silently when zero events make the hazard ratio undefined. A reader receives no risk difference or absolute risk under the intervention, so the number reported is not the quantity the protocol defined.
problems.quote: Hazard ratios were estimated using weighted Cox proportional hazards models, except when no event were observed in one group.

problems.evidence: Residual confounding is acknowledged and then argued away qualitatively, by noting that subclavian patients were four years older and that this would bias against subclavian access. No negative control outcome, no proxy for operator skill and no validation subsample enters the analysis, and the two sensitivity analyses vary eligibility restriction and catheter rank rather than the untestable assumption.
problems.quote: Then, despite the application of causal inference methods, residual unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Target trial emulation to estimate the effects of lifestyle interventions on mortality among cancer survivors: an editorial commentary.
papers.one_line: An editorial on a three-step framework for emulating lifestyle guideline adherence in breast and prostate cancer survivors shows that the operationalized protocol dropped the guidelines' leading recommendation, achieve and maintain a healthy weight, in a population where over 70% of survivors carry overweight or obesity.
papers.what_was_done: The framework under discussion estimates the mortality effect of adhering to the WCRF-AICR and ACS diet and physical activity guidelines among breast and prostate cancer survivors in the Nurses' Health Studies I and II and the Health Professionals Follow-Up Study. The operationalization drops the first recommendation of both guideline sets, achieve and maintain a healthy weight, in a survivor population where more than 70% have a body mass index in the overweight or obese range and where both breast cancer and aggressive prostate cancer are obesity-related. Separate aerobic and muscle-strengthening recommendations are collapsed into one adherence variable, sedentary behavior is absent, and the sex-specific red meat limits (under 18 oz per week for men, under 12 oz per week for women) are argued not to preserve the guidelines' intent. Survivors are censored on ever experiencing stroke or myocardial infarction on the assumption that adherence becomes impossible, and survivors with gout, type 2 diabetes or difficulty climbing a flight of stairs are excluded or excused, though these are the people behavioral intervention trials target. Against the claim that long-term randomized trials here are impractical, the CHALLENGE trial randomized 889 resected colon cancer patients to structured exercise or health education, with 7.9 years median follow-up, disease-free survival hazard ratio 0.72 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.94, P = 0.017) and overall survival 0.63 (95% CI 0.43 to 0.94, P = 0.022). Exposure measurement in the cohorts occurs at arbitrary times relative to the cancer treatment sequence.

future_research.gap: Observational cohorts are not measured at the timepoints that would let an emulation address a clinically actionable question
future_research.quote: Without lifestyle assessments at these clinically relevant time points, it is not possible to apply target trial emulation to answer clinically relevant questions about lifestyle and survival.
future_research.locator: Target trial emulation studies need to answer clinically relevant questions

problems.evidence: The scientific target is adherence to two named guideline sets; the emulated protocol is what the cohort data could carry, and the gap between them includes the guidelines' first recommendation in a population where over 70% of survivors are overweight or obese. The published estimate is a single mortality contrast with no term separating the loss from dropping weight management, the loss from merging aerobic with muscle-strengthening exercise, and estimation error. A reader is asked to interpret the number as the effect of following the guidelines.
problems.quote: the leading diet and physical activity recommendation of both the WCRF-AICR and the ACS is to “Achieve and maintain a healthy weight”

problems.evidence: Aerobic and muscle-strengthening exercise are separate recommendations in the source guidelines and are combined into one adherence indicator, sedentary behavior is left out entirely, and the sex-specific red meat limits are operationalized in a way argued not to preserve the guidelines' intent. Two survivors with the same adherence value can therefore have done different things, and no procedure states which behavior combinations are members of the same treatment version.
problems.quote: the decisions regarding guideline adherence also do not acknowledge the separate guidelines for aerobic and muscle-strengthening exercise (which are combined in this analysis)

problems.evidence: The intervention is guideline adherence, a bundle of diet, alcohol and physical activity behaviors with no assignment unit, no dose, no delivery mechanism and no comparator regimen. Where a randomized version exists it looks nothing like the emulated contrast: CHALLENGE delivered a three-year structured exercise program against health education materials in 889 patients and reported a disease-free survival hazard ratio of 0.72. The emulated strategy has no such specification, and the compromises that made it estimable are exactly where the treatment versions went undefined.
problems.quote: Most existing observational studies have not been designed with target trial emulation in mind.
problems.locator: Target trial emulation studies need to answer clinically relevant questions

problems.evidence: Time zero and the exposure window are set by when the parent cohorts happened to mail their questionnaires, not by any clinically meaningful point in the treatment sequence. The measurement schedule is described as arbitrary relative to diagnosis, and the question that matters clinically, whether the behavior occurred immediately before, during, between or after a treatment combination, cannot be posed at all because no assessment lands there.
problems.quote: often are performed at arbitrary time points well before or after the cancer diagnosis rather than at clinically important time points in relation to cancer treatments
problems.locator: Target trial emulation studies need to answer clinically relevant questions

problems.evidence: Survivors are censored at any stroke or myocardial infarction under the assumption that adherence afterward is impossible, which is an identifying assumption about the post-event adherence process presented as an eligibility housekeeping rule. Standard care after those events is cardiac rehabilitation, where physical activity and a plant-based diet are emphasized rather than abandoned, so the censoring rule contradicts the mechanism it invokes and removes person-time in which the strategy is most plausibly followed.
problems.quote: ever experiencing these events is grounds for censoring under an assumption that these individuals may be unable to continue adherence to guidelines

problems.evidence: Survivors with type 2 diabetes, gout or functional limitation are excluded or excused, and comorbidity and functional limitation are highly prevalent among cancer survivors, so the estimated population is a fit subset of the population the guidelines address. Nothing in the analysis transports the estimate from that subset back to the survivor population it is offered for, and the sampling assumption that would be required is not stated alongside the confounding assumptions.
problems.quote: we worry that the estimates reported in this paper may be ungeneralizable to the greater population of survivors for which this work is intended

problems.evidence: Deciding whether the causal reading is tenable is described as difficult and largely subjective, informed by triangulation and negative controls, and the editorial concludes it cannot accept the estimates as causal while praising the technical execution. The published report supplies safeguards against unmeasured confounding and positivity but no structure that separates the assumptions a reader can check from the ones nobody can, which is why two competent groups can read the same analysis and disagree on its standing.
problems.quote: describe this step as difficult and largely subjective
problems.locator: Is a causal interpretation of the analyses tenable?

papers.title: Synthetic target trial emulation and predictive modeling of amylin-pathway therapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes.
papers.one_line: Synthetic individual patient data were generated from the published summary statistics of seven randomized trials (N = 5,786) and then used for g-formula head-to-head causal contrasts, dose-response optimization and machine learning response prediction reported at 82 to 87 percent accuracy.
papers.what_was_done: Seven randomized trials of amylin-pathway therapies published up to September 2025, totaling 5,786 participants, were located by systematic search and their aggregate results extracted. Synthetic individual patient data were then constructed to match those aggregates: baseline covariates from multivariate normal distributions matched to reported means, standard deviations and correlations, longitudinal trajectories from mixed-effects models fit to visit-wise summaries, responder outcomes from beta-binomial distributions constrained to reported responder rates, and adverse events from time-to-event distributions calibrated to published cumulative incidence curves. Fidelity was checked against the same published aggregates: means within 0.1 percent, standard deviations within 10 percent relative difference, responder rates within 0.3 percentage points and trajectory R-squared above 0.95. The synthetic records were then treated as a cohort for target trial emulation, with harmonized eligibility, a common time zero at dose escalation, g-formula assignment, E-values for unmeasured confounding, and Bayesian network meta-analysis. Reported outputs include an ED80 for subcutaneous amycretin of 8.88 mg (95% CI 7.12 to 11.08), a CagriSema posterior probability of superiority above 0.95, plateau timing at 52 to 68 weeks for obesity endpoints, and phase III sample sizes of 800 to 1,200 per arm for 90 percent power. Nausea rates at three untested doses (2.5, 7.5 and 20 mg) were imputed rather than observed. Leave-trial-out cross-validation gave an efficacy root mean square error of 2.9 percentage points and a calibration slope of 0.61.

future_research.gap: Imputed dose-stratified adverse event rates at untested doses drive the benefit-risk window and are not empirically grounded
future_research.quote: these remain informed estimates pending empirical validation

future_research.gap: Re-weighting to a target population interpolates within the observed covariate space and is not external validation
future_research.quote: but this represents interpolation within the observed covariate space rather than true external validation

problems.evidence: The entire evidence base is generated data, validated exclusively on distributional agreement with the published aggregates it was built from: means within 0.1 percent, standard deviations within 10 percent, trajectory R-squared above 0.95. That check cannot fail by construction, because the generator was constrained to those same statistics. The generated records are then used for causal contrasts across trials, dose optimization and individual response prediction, which are exactly the uses that distributional fidelity does not license.
problems.quote: We verified that synthetic data reproduced primary endpoint means within 0.1 %, standard deviations within 10 % relative difference, responder rates within 0.3 % points, correlation structures within 0.05 units, and trajectory shapes with R 2 values.
problems.locator: Methods, synthetic individual patient data reconstruction

problems.evidence: No head-to-head trial of CagriSema against subcutaneous amycretin exists, and the missing comparison is supplied by g-formula assignment over synthetic records plus Bayesian network meta-analysis, producing a posterior probability of superiority above 0.95. The identification problem, that the compared arms come from different trials with different protocols, is unchanged by the modeling; the flexibility of the estimation stack is what is offered in its place, together with E-values applied to contrasts that were never observed.
problems.quote: Virtual head-to-head comparisons allowed for causal inference across trials never directly compared

problems.evidence: The label target trial emulation is applied to a reanalysis of seven published trial summaries with no patient-level data at all, and the protocol vocabulary of eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment and causal contrasts is filled in over generated records. The result is offered for regulatory submissions and payer negotiations, so the design label is doing the work of an assumption audit for a dataset in which no individual observation exists.
problems.quote: Assignment procedures utilized the g-formula approach to estimate effects under hypothetical randomization to different treatment strategies.
problems.locator: Methods, synthetic target trial emulation framework

problems.evidence: Machine learning models are reported to predict treatment response from baseline characteristics at 82 to 87 percent accuracy, and population enrichment strategies are proposed on that basis. The same document states that the reconstruction preserves only the reported constraints and cannot support subgroup heterogeneity that the source trials did not pre-specify, so the individual-level signal the models are learning is the correlation structure the generator was told to impose, not evidence about who benefits.
problems.quote: this method cannot support analyses requiring patient-level interaction terms or subgroup heterogeneity not pre-specified in original trials

problems.evidence: Estimates built from mainly North American and European trial populations with baseline BMI 31 to 38 kg/m2 are re-calibrated to a target population at roughly 37 kg/m2 using arm-normalized Mahalanobis kernel weights, and the transport step is then acknowledged to be interpolation inside the observed covariate space. The sampling assumptions of that reweighting are stacked on top of a synthetic data-generating assumption and an across-trial exchangeability assumption, and no accounting separates the three contributions to the reported uncertainty.
problems.quote: but this represents interpolation within the observed covariate space rather than true external validation

problems.evidence: Unmeasured confounding is addressed with E-values computed one contrast at a time, while the analysis simultaneously assumes that generated records carry the joint distribution of the source populations, that eligibility harmonization made trials exchangeable, and that imputed nausea rates at 2.5, 7.5 and 20 mg are correct. The imputation sensitivity analysis alone shifts the optimal window by plus or minus 2 mg, and no analysis varies more than one of these assumptions at a time.
problems.quote: Fourth, we assessed potential for unmeasured confounding through E-value calculations quantifying the minimum strength of unmeasured confounding required to nullify observed effects.
problems.locator: Methods, synthetic target trial emulation framework

papers.title: Type 2 diabetes, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes: real world evidence versus a randomised clinical trial.
papers.one_line: A Danish register emulation of EMPA-REG using longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimation reports a three-year MACE risk difference of 2.8 percentage points for continuous SGLT2i, an estimand of uninterrupted treatment in a cohort where 53% had stopped by 36 months.
papers.what_was_done: Seven Danish nationwide registries identified 116,823 people who first redeemed an SGLT2i or DPP4i prescription between 2013 and 2021; EMPA-REG eligibility left 13,524 (SGLT2i 6,025, DPP4i 7,499). Follow-up was split into six-month intervals and the estimand was the absolute risk difference under three years of continuous treatment, estimated by longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimation with nuisance models fitted as penalized elastic nets undersmoothed to the lowest penalty at which they converged, without truncation of propensity or censoring probabilities, and with cheap bootstrap confidence intervals. At 36 months MACE risk was 11.5% with SGLT2i against 14.2% with DPP4i, a difference of 2.8 percentage points (95% CI 1.1 to 4.4); heart failure hospitalization differed by 5.1 points (4.3 to 6.0), all-cause mortality by 3.1 points (1.5 to 4.7), cardiovascular death by 1.4 points (0.3 to 2.5) and stroke by 2.4 points (1.7 to 3.1). Non-adherence to the initiating drug reached 53% for SGLT2i and 52% for DPP4i by 36 months. EMPA-REG reports hazard ratios and no absolute risks, so the trial comparison was constructed by reading its Kaplan-Meier curves with PlotDigitizer, giving a trial MACE difference of about 1.6% against the emulation's 2.8% and a heart failure difference of about 1.4% against 5.1%. Calendar-year stratification as a sensitivity analysis cut the population to 7,590 and left MACE at 3.1 points.

problems.evidence: The estimand is three years of uninterrupted treatment in a population where 53% of SGLT2i and 52% of DPP4i initiators had stopped by 36 months, so the counterfactual is supported by the minority who persisted, conditional on six intervals of evolving comorbidity. Propensity and censoring probabilities were deliberately left untruncated and the nuisance fits deliberately undersmoothed, which maximizes the influence of the least supported histories. What the report shows is risk curves and confidence intervals, not which treatment and covariate histories have no support at interval five or six.
problems.quote: We did not truncate propensity scores and censoring probabilities.

problems.evidence: The trial comparison had to be manufactured because EMPA-REG publishes hazard ratios and no absolute risks, so its Kaplan-Meier curves were digitized to produce the numbers being compared against. The resulting pairs are far apart, 5.1 versus roughly 1.4 percentage points for heart failure hospitalization and 2.8 versus roughly 1.6 for MACE, and the difference is narrated as real-world benefit rather than quantified as calibration error between two estimands that differ in effect measure, adherence handling and population.
problems.quote: The EMPA-REG OUTCOME trial does not report absolute risks. These were obtained by using PlotDigitizer to inspect their Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves.
problems.locator: Comparison to the EMPA-REG Outcome trial

problems.evidence: The comparison that carries the conclusion places a three-year continuous-treatment risk difference of 2.8 percentage points against a trial hazard ratio, and the mismatch is acknowledged as complicating direct comparison and then worked around by digitizing curves. The trial estimand is intention-to-treat and the emulation estimand conditions on uninterrupted treatment through 53% discontinuation, so the two quantities answer different questions and neither is converted into the other's scale.
problems.quote: However, EMPA-REG reports hazard ratios rather than absolute risks or relative risks, complicating direct comparisons.

problems.evidence: A nationwide cohort of 116,823 first-time users becomes 13,524 after EMPA-REG eligibility, an 88% loss before any weighting. The calendar-year balanced enrollment sensitivity analysis halves that again to 7,590, and subgroup estimates are then read off strata of the smaller number, including a MACE difference of 0.2 percentage points (95% CI minus 2.0 to 2.3) under 65 years. The database size that motivates the study is not the size that supports the estimate.
problems.quote: Sensitivity analyses, accounting for temporal effects via stratification by calendar year, reduced the population to 7,590 patients.

problems.evidence: Calendar-time confounding is real here and is measured: DPP4i initiation dominated 2013 to 2015 while SGLT2i initiation rose later, so drug choice is confounded with era of care. The response is a sampling algorithm that enrolls equal numbers of each initiator per calendar year, and the MACE estimate moves only from 2.8 to 3.1 percentage points, which is a genuine diagnostic that few emulations run. It does not address repeated participation, since each person enters once, and it costs 44% of the sample, so the procedure is available but its price is not costed against the bias it removes.
problems.quote: Our sampling algorithm enrolled an equal number of people who initiated SGLT2i and DPP4i into the emulated trial in each calendar year, maintaining balanced representation of both treatments over time.

problems.evidence: The nuisance models depart from prediction-optimal tuning on purpose: elastic net penalties are pushed down to undersmooth the fits, which is the recognized direction of correction when the target is a causal parameter rather than a prediction. The criterion that stops the descent is numerical, the lowest penalty at which the model still converged, not any measure of causal performance, and with six intervals of treatment, censoring and outcome models there is no report of how the choice affected the estimate.
problems.quote: All nuisance parameter models were fitted using penalized elastic nets where the penalty parameters were chosen such as to undersmooth the regression fits, that is the lowest penalty value where the model still converged.

problems.evidence: Inference for a longitudinal targeted minimum loss estimate over six intervals in 13,524 people is delivered by cheap bootstrapping, a procedure designed to avoid refitting the whole estimator on every resample, and it is what makes the confidence intervals computable at all. It is stated in one clause with no report of resample count, no comparison against the influence-function standard error the estimator supplies, and no coverage check, so the scalable option is used without evidence that it is correct here.
problems.quote: Confidence intervals were calculated by cheap bootstrapping

problems.evidence: Death is not silently censored for the cause-specific endpoints: competing risks are stated to have been accounted for, and all-cause mortality is reported alongside cardiovascular death, so the reader can see both. What is not stated is which estimand that choice implies, cause-specific hazard or subdistribution risk, nor the assumption it rests on, and the sentence doing the work is seven words long in a paper that otherwise details its estimator at length.
problems.quote: For cause specific deaths competing risks have been accounted for.

papers.title: Trastuzumab in early curative breast cancer: A target trial emulation benchmarked against two randomized clinical trials.
papers.one_line: A Swedish register emulation of the B-31 and N9831 trastuzumab trials in 1,578 women declares benchmarking successful on qualitative agreement of direction alone, after deciding in advance not to compare effect measures with the trials quantitatively.
papers.what_was_done: The Swedish National Quality Register for Breast Cancer linked to seven further national registers supplied 1,578 women diagnosed between 2008 and 2015 for an emulation of the jointly analyzed B-31 and N9831 trials of adjuvant trastuzumab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone. Because the two strategies were not distinguishable at baseline, all but 308 individuals were cloned into both arms, censored on deviation, and reweighted with time-varying inverse probability weights truncated at the 99th percentile, with 500 bootstrap samples for confidence intervals. Five-year disease-free survival was 74.7% (95% CI 70.7 to 78.5) with trastuzumab against 53.5% (46.6 to 60.3) without, a risk difference of minus 21.2% (minus 29.2 to minus 13.8) and risk ratio 0.54 (0.44 to 0.67); overall survival was 90.7% against 67.5%, a risk difference of minus 23.2% and risk ratio 0.29 (0.20 to 0.40), considerably larger than the trials. The trials reported hazard ratios, so the comparison was declared to be qualitative from the outset. The protocol deviated from the trials by dropping the life-expectancy criterion and by identifying eligibility from prior clinical events and drug use instead of biomarkers such as ejection fraction, and treatment strategies used a 12-week window plus a 2-week grace period. Local recurrence was operationalized as a surgical procedure code and distant recurrence as a secondary-cancer code. The start date of chemotherapy was missing for 20% of individuals and was imputed by Bayesian linear regression. Analysis code is published on GitHub; the register data are not shareable.

future_research.gap: Discontinuation and dose modification data that the per-protocol analysis needs do not exist in the registers
future_research.quote: Also, we would need information on treatment discontinuation and dose modifications, which is not captured in the registers.

problems.evidence: The comparison rule was fixed before the estimates existed and it is a direction test, adopted because the trials reported hazard ratios and the emulation reports risk differences. What that rule cannot see is the size of the disagreement it passes: the emulation's overall survival risk difference of minus 23.2% is described as considerably larger than the trials' effect and benchmarking is still recorded as successful. The verdict is a label, and the interval that would say how far apart the two estimands are is never computed.
problems.quote: Therefore, instead of comparing the effect measures quantitatively, the focus would be on qualitatively evaluating the direction of effects and overall conclusions to decide whether benchmarking was successful.

problems.evidence: Success on trastuzumab in HER2-positive breast cancer is offered as grounds for trusting Swedish register data on questions the trials could not answer, specifically older and underrepresented patients and subgroup heterogeneity. Nothing connects the two: the questions being licensed are the ones where the trials' eligibility criteria and the registers' recording practices differ most, and the emulation's own protocol had to drop the life-expectancy criterion and substitute clinical events for ejection fraction to run at all.
problems.quote: it would increase confidence in the ability of these data to ask questions that could not be answered in the initial trial

problems.evidence: The explanation offered for the emulation's larger overall survival effect is that chemotherapy-arm participants in the trials crossed over to trastuzumab, attenuating the trials' intention-to-treat estimate, while the emulation censors on deviation and estimates a per-protocol analogue. The two numbers therefore diverge by an amount that grows with follow-up and with comparator-arm uptake, and the qualitative benchmarking rule counts the pair as agreeing because both favor trastuzumab.
problems.quote: If individuals assigned to the chemotherapy arm in the trials switched to additionally receive trastuzumab, this could lead to an attenuation of the effect estimate on overall survival in an intention-to-treat analysis.

problems.evidence: The trials excluded patients on ejection fraction and on life expectancy under ten years; the registers hold neither, so eligibility was rebuilt from prior diagnoses and dispensed drugs and the life-expectancy criterion was dropped. The emulated population is thus defined by what Swedish registers record about healthcare contact rather than by cardiac function, which is a different eligible set, not a mismeasured version of the trials' one, and the cardiac criterion was the one that governed who could safely receive the drug under study.
problems.quote: relevant eligibility criteria would be identified using prior clinical events and drug use rather than biomarker levels

problems.evidence: Local recurrence is present in the data only if a surgeon removed it, and distant recurrence is a secondary-cancer code that can equally represent a local or regional event. Both enter the composite disease-free survival endpoint as error-free binary variables, and the argument that misclassification is tolerable because components absorb each other's errors applies to the composite while leaving the component estimates uninterpretable. No sensitivity or specificity is estimated for either phenotype.
problems.quote: we defined local recurrences using surgical procedure codes, meaning a local recurrence that was not removed is missed

problems.evidence: The treatment strategy is initiation within 12 weeks of chemotherapy with a 2-week grace period, and clones are censored at week 14 if trastuzumab has not started. Neither the 12-week window nor the 2-week grace period is derived from any rule, and the sensitivity analysis that varies them uses weeks 8 to 16, another unmotivated pair of boundaries. Since the grace period determines who remains uncensored, it determines the population the per-protocol estimate describes.
problems.quote: initiation of trastuzumab within 12 weeks (plus a 2-week grace period to consider delays in treatment) after receiving chemotherapy

problems.evidence: A negative control outcome is actually used: the null result for other second primary cancers is read as evidence against unmeasured confounding in the cancer-specific endpoints. The control was not prespecified as one; it is a component of the study's own composite endpoint reinterpreted after the fact, it is not calibrated into a bias adjustment of the reported risk differences, and it is not accompanied by any proxy or validation data. The frailty pathway that would explain the outsized overall survival effect is precisely the one a second-primary-cancer control cannot rule out.
problems.quote: if we consider the null result for other second primary cancers as a negative control to assess the impact of potential unmeasured factors

problems.evidence: Variance after cloning, censoring and time-varying weighting is handled by nonparametric bootstrap with 500 resamples, which is a correct default and is reported. It is also the reason the approach does not generalize: 500 refits of a pooled logistic model with time-varying weights over 1,578 individuals is affordable, and the same procedure over a sequence-expanded national cohort is not. No analytic or scalable alternative is offered, and the bootstrap count is not justified against the width of the resulting intervals.
problems.quote: Nonparametric bootstrapping with 500 samples was used to calculate 95% confidence intervals.
problems.locator: The observational emulation of the target trial

papers.title: Target trial emulation: harnessing real-world data to evaluate surgery and perioperative care interventions.
papers.one_line: A surgical editorial positioning target trial emulation as the route from registry data to technology appraisal reports that the funded feasibility work could not specify time zero from routine data and concludes that confounding by indication persists no matter how well the framework is applied.
papers.what_was_done: The case for emulation in surgery rests on the failure rate of surgical trials, with as many as 20% of surgical randomized trials discontinued early for recruitment and funding reasons, and on external validity evidence, a review of 307 vascular surgery randomized trials finding significant demographic and clinical differences between recruited patients and the real-world population. Against that, the National Institute of Health and Care Excellence real-world evidence framework is cited as the policy vehicle, with the FDA and EMA producing parallel guidance and PRINCIPLED offered as the process guide. Feasibility has been demonstrated in a narrow band: the NIHR-funded Emergency Surgery or Not study is named as proof that target trials of selected conditions can be run on routine data in a small group of highly selected surgical conditions and interventions. The obstacles reported from that work are specific: routinely collected data lacked the variables needed to specify time zero, intention-to-treat status and residual confounding; registries do not capture patients turned down for surgery; and matching-based emulations discard large numbers of participants. Replication against randomized trials is described as having succeeded in a small number of selected surgical and non-surgical populations, at a fraction of trial cost and time.

future_research.gap: Whether appraisal decisions can rest on emulation, and how to read the results, is unresolved
future_research.quote: Further research is required to demonstrate the feasibility of basing healthcare decisions and technology appraisals on observational studies employing TTE, and how to interpret the associated results.

future_research.gap: Registries would have to change what they collect for emulation to be possible
future_research.quote: Surgical and perioperative care registries should consider integrating TTE elements into data collection to enable RWD research with robust causal inference methodologies.

problems.evidence: The funded feasibility programme found that routine surgical data lack the variables needed to specify time zero and treatment assignment, and data quality is named as the barrier to using emulation in formal technology appraisals. What is absent is any statement of how much variable coverage would be enough: the assessment is a list of things that were missing in one study, with no threshold that would tell a future team to stop before analysis rather than report the shortfall afterward.
problems.quote: several challenges were identified, including a lack of specific data variables within the routinely collected RWD to enable stringent specification of some TTE components, including the determination of time zero

problems.evidence: Emulation is recommended inside the NICE real-world evidence framework and has already influenced national technology appraisals, yet whether appraisal decisions can rest on it is stated to require further research, including how to interpret the results. Regulators are therefore already receiving this evidence class without a criterion for adequate emulation or acceptable residual confounding, and the recommendation offered is a reporting guideline rather than a threshold.
problems.quote: Further research is required to demonstrate the feasibility of basing healthcare decisions and technology appraisals on observational studies employing TTE, and how to interpret the associated results.

problems.evidence: The framework is presented as the method that makes routine surgical data reliable, and the same paragraph states that confounding by indication defeats reliability regardless of how well the framework is applied. Applying the label therefore certifies nothing about the assumption burden of a surgical comparison, where the reason a patient was operated on is the strongest determinant of outcome and is rarely recorded.
problems.quote: Due to the lack of true randomization, intractable confounding and confounding by indication hinder the reliability of results, no matter how well the TTE framework is applied

problems.evidence: The argument for routine surgical data is large sample size containing clinically important subgroups, and the acknowledged cost of the design is that matching discards a significant number of participants. The sample that survives eligibility, comparator restriction and matching is what carries the estimate, and no reported quantity in a surgical emulation tells a reader what that number is or which subgroups it kept.
problems.quote: TTEs employing a matching approach to compare similarly matched groups can result in the loss of a significant number of participants.

problems.evidence: Surgical registries record procedures, so a patient assessed and turned down for surgery generates no registry entry at all. Eligibility for the emulated trial is then defined over a population selected on having received the treatment being studied, which conditions on a healthcare-use variable downstream of both indication and prognosis. The comparator arm of a surgery versus no surgery emulation is missing by construction rather than by chance.
problems.quote: Inherent selection biases of the dataset itself (for example, many registries do not capture patients turned down for surgery) and missing covariates may limit the ability to emulate the ‘ideal’ target trial

problems.evidence: Replication is reported as having worked in a small number of selected surgical and non-surgical populations, and that record is the stated basis for proposing emulation as the route to guideline development and technology appraisal across surgery. No argument connects the questions that replicated to the questions being proposed, and the specific obstacles listed, missing time zero variables and registries that omit non-operated patients, are properties of the new questions rather than of the ones that replicated.
problems.quote: It has replicated the findings of RCTs with very similar effect estimates in a small number of selected surgical and non-surgical populations

papers.title: Target trial emulation on dexmedetomidine for critically ill patients: all that glitters is not gold.
papers.one_line: A commentary on an intensive care emulation of dexmedetomidine for agitation, where 314 treated and 1,738 untreated patients yielded 93% versus 72.1% agitation resolution, notes that the early-initiation group driving the contrast is smaller still and never counted.
papers.what_was_done: The emulation under discussion drew consecutive adult intensive care admissions from 2016 to 2021 and identified agitation by natural language processing over electronic medical record text. The treatment strategy was administration of dexmedetomidine within 30 days of agitation onset, giving 314 treated and 1,738 untreated patients, with resolution of agitation within 30 days as the outcome. The headline contrast is not the 30-day strategy but early use within 12 hours, reported as roughly 93% resolution against 72.1% among those who never received the drug. The size of that 12-hour group is not reported anywhere in the emulation. Mean dexmedetomidine doses of 0.56 mg/kg/h (0.34 to 0.87) are set against SPICE III doses of 0.54 mg/kg/hour (0.35 to 0.72) under 65 years and 0.44 mg/kg/hour (0.27 to 0.64) over 65 years, undercutting the argument that the drug was not being used as a sedative. The surrounding randomized evidence is not thin: a meta-analysis of 77 randomized trials in 11,997 critically ill patients, plus SPICE III and ADRESS showing increased mortality signals.

future_research.gap: The estimate is not treated as decision-grade evidence given the existing randomized base
future_research.quote: we agree with the authors, the study should be considered hypothesis-generating until better evidence is provided

problems.evidence: A consecutive five-year intensive care population reduces to 314 treated patients, and the contrast that is actually reported, 93% versus 72.1%, rests on the subset who started within 12 hours of onset. That subset is smaller again and its size is never given, so a reader cannot tell how many patients support the headline number. The commentary has to infer the shortage rather than read it, which is what an unreported effective sample looks like.
problems.quote: Firstly, the sample size of patients using dexmedetomidine was small and even smaller -though unmentioned by the authors - was the group that began its use within 12 hours.

problems.evidence: Two time windows carry the analysis and neither is justified: a 30-day window for counting initiation as adherence to the strategy, and a 12-hour cutoff that defines the early group whose 93% resolution is the reported finding. Agitation resolution within 30 days is also the outcome, so the initiation window and the outcome window coincide. No outcome-blind rule selects either boundary.
problems.quote: an intervention was identified, which was the administration of dexmedetomidine within 30 days of onset of agitation

problems.evidence: Eligibility for the emulated trial is a text-mining phenotype: terms and expressions in medical records taken to indicate agitation. Both the eligibility criterion and the outcome, resolution of agitation, come from the same documentation stream, so a patient sedated early stops generating agitation text and is recorded as resolved. The phenotype enters as an error-free binary variable with no validation against bedside assessment and no sensitivity or specificity reported.
problems.quote: Natural Language Processing was utilized to search for terms, words, or expressions in electronic medical records indicating agitation to identify eligible patients.

problems.evidence: The emulation is described as advanced methodology replicating a randomized trial, and the commentary has to argue back that the design label does not change the assumption burden or the standing of the result against 77 randomized trials in 11,997 patients. The conditions under which observational evidence should substitute for a trial, cost, infeasibility, ethics or urgency, are noted to be absent here, so the label alone is what promoted the analysis.
problems.quote: Thirdly, although TTE is a robust approach to designing and analyzing observational studies, it does not replace or dismiss the importance of conducting a well-designed clinical trial.

problems.evidence: The protocol defines a strategy of initiation within 30 days, which makes the estimand a contrast over everyone compatible with that window, but the number carried into the conclusion is a within-12-hour comparison against never-treated patients. A quantity estimated among an early-initiating subset is being read as the effect of the declared strategy, and the two differ in both the population and the intervention they describe.
problems.quote: The authors found that early dexmedetomidine use (i.e., within 12 hours) led to the resolution of agitation in approximately 93% of patients, compared to 72.1% in those who never received dexmedetomidine.

papers.title: Strengthening health technology assessment for cancer treatments in Europe by integrating causal inference and target trial emulation.
papers.one_line: A methodological argument that EU joint clinical assessment should admit causal inference and target trial emulation, noting that between 2015 and 2020 the FDA approved 43% and the EMA 21% of non-orphan drugs on single-arm studies while HTA bodies rejected external-control submissions outright or diverged among themselves.
papers.what_was_done: The EU health technology assessment guidelines that took effect in 2025 for all new cancer drugs place their methodological weight on meta-analysis of direct and indirect comparisons of randomized trials, which is set against the approval record: 43% of FDA and 21% of EMA non-orphan approvals between 2015 and 2020 rested on single-arm studies with no control arm. Survey evidence from Germany, France and the United Kingdom is cited showing that reimbursement applications based on external controls were rejected entirely or handled divergently across bodies. The argument runs through the three steps of causal inference, specification of the estimand, identification and estimation, and reviews propensity score matching, inverse probability weighting, the g-computation formula and g-estimation as the estimation options, with the ICH estimand attributes named as the missing piece of the PICO framework. Target trial emulation is presented as the design vehicle, with time zero alignment, the option of a new trial at each eligible timepoint, cloning with censoring, and a grace period illustrated at three months. Exchangeability, positivity and consistency are stated to be untestable and to require justification from theory. The prescription for adequacy is qualitative throughout: excellent observational data, high cohort data quality, a full set of all known covariates, regular follow-up and adjudicated outcomes.

future_research.gap: The data infrastructure that would make emulation admissible for reimbursement decisions does not exist
future_research.quote: Creation of a real-world database infrastructure of high quality and granularity is an absolute priority to advance HTA

problems.evidence: The state of reimbursement decision making is documented as either a blanket rejection of external-control evidence or divergence among national bodies facing the same submission, which is what the absence of a threshold looks like in practice. Nothing in the EU guidelines that took effect in 2025 for every new cancer drug states how much residual confounding is acceptable or what would count as an adequate emulation, and the proposal that follows adds methods without adding a criterion.
problems.quote: applications and approvals for reimbursement of cancer drugs that were based on external controls were entirely rejected
problems.locator: European union health technology assessment methodological guidelines for joint clinical assessments

problems.evidence: The condition placed on using emulation for reimbursement decisions is that the data be excellent, elsewhere expanded to a well characterized cohort with a full set of all known covariates at baseline, regular and maximally complete follow-up, and adjudicated outcomes. Not one of those phrases carries a measurable threshold, so an assessor receiving a dossier has no test that would return a refusal, and this is a proposal aimed at regulators who need exactly such a test.
problems.quote: Therefore, causal inference and target trial emulation should become an option for comparative effectiveness research if excellent observational data is available.

problems.evidence: Exchangeability, positivity and consistency are correctly identified as untestable and are handed to the reader as a narrative to be checked by argument. The remedy proposed is transparency of statement, not a structured report that separates the assumptions an analyst can diagnose from the ones nobody can, so an assessment panel reading two dossiers cannot see which one carries the heavier undiagnosable burden.
problems.quote: These assumptions cannot be tested statistically but rather must be justified based on theory

problems.evidence: The grace period is introduced as a device that g-methods permit and is illustrated at three months with no rule for choosing it, and the same passage offers a new trial at each timepoint or at prespecified selected timepoints as alternatives without a criterion for selecting between them. In a document written to give assessors a methodological basis for reimbursement decisions, a design parameter that moves the estimand is left to the analyst.
problems.quote: G-methods allows also for the definition of a grace period after time 0 (e.g. 3 months) during which initiation of a treatment is still considered acceptable.

problems.evidence: The case made to HTA bodies is that emulation and g-estimation avoid or minimize known biases, which converts the design label into the argument for admissibility. The unmeasured confounding assumption is stated a few paragraphs earlier to be untestable, so the label carries no information about the assumption burden of any particular dossier, yet it is the basis on which a class of evidence is proposed for reimbursement decisions covering all EU member states.
problems.quote: Target trial emulation and g-estimation are valid tools to model causal contrast of treatments by avoiding or minimizing well-knowns bias in observational study protocol development and conduct.

papers.title: The R.O.A.D. to clinical trial emulation.
papers.one_line: A framework that matches an observational cohort to a target trial's reported covariate means and control-arm prognosis, then reweights the treated arm until the estimated survival equals the trial's treated-arm survival, and describes the last step as eliminating unobserved confounding.
papers.what_was_done: An observational cohort of 779 patients with colorectal liver metastases resected between 2002 and 2019 across the IGCLM consortium, 639 untreated and 140 treated, was filtered to the eligibility criteria of the JCOG0603 randomized trial. An optimization then selected 216 patients, 108 per arm, chosen so that the mean predicted baseline recurrence risk and the four covariate means reported in the trial's published table matched the trial. Baseline risk was predicted by a machine learning model trained on untreated patients; the counterfactual survival models reached an in-sample C-index of 0.88 against cross-validated C-indices of 0.68 untreated and 0.61 treated. After matching, the treated arm's five-year recurrence-free survival was 11 percentage points below the trial's 49%, and a cost-sensitive weight of 1.5 on treated patients without recurrence was applied until the estimate matched the trial; a weight of 1.25 was applied to untreated non-recurrent patients for the same purpose. Optimal policy trees were then trained on the reweighted cohort, assigning 186 of 216 patients to benefit under the first tree, with a reward constraint set at 0.78 chosen as the largest value that still permitted a split. Absence of confounding within tree nodes was declared on the basis that two external prognostic scores gave similar baseline risk in each arm. The outcome is recurrence-free survival because secondary cancers are not recorded in the observational data, while the trial endpoint was disease-free survival.

problems.evidence: The identification failure is named correctly: after matching, the treated arm's five-year recurrence-free survival sat 11 percentage points below the trial's 49%, and that gap is attributed to unobserved confounding. The response is a cost-sensitive loss with a weight of 1.5 on treated patients who did not recur, tuned until the model output equals the trial number. A weight chosen to make an estimate hit a target does not identify anything; it moves a prediction, and the claim that this eliminates the confounding is a claim that estimation flexibility substitutes for identification.
problems.quote: By adjusting the weight such that h ˆ t = 1 = μ 1 , we eliminate the effect of the unobserved confounding.
problems.locator: Methods, cost-sensitive counterfactual models and reward estimation

problems.evidence: Both arms of the emulation are tuned to the trial before any comparison: weight 1.5 for treated non-recurrent patients and 1.25 for untreated non-recurrent patients, each applied until the predicted survival matched the corresponding trial arm. Agreement with JCOG0603 is then reported as validation, at the level of direction, significance and rough effect size. A comparison whose inputs were fitted to the answer cannot be a calibrated comparison of estimands, and the binary verdict of successful emulation is the only thing the procedure can return.
problems.quote: we applied a weight of 1.5 for treated patients with no recurrence, which improved the predicted 5-year RFS, now matching that reported in the treated group of the target RCT

problems.evidence: The confounding check applies two external prognostic scores, the MSK clinical risk score and the JHH GAME score, within each policy tree node and concludes there is no confounding because predicted baseline risk is similar across arms. Balance on the predictions of models built from measured prognostic factors is by definition a statement about measured confounding, and it is used here to license a conclusion about unmeasured confounding. No negative control outcome, no proxy variable and no validation sample enters anywhere in the pipeline.
problems.quote: the absence of observed confounding in these nodes would provide reasonable evidence that unobserved confounding is also absent
problems.locator: Methods, validation of absence of confounding

problems.evidence: The trial endpoint is disease-free survival, which includes secondary cancers; the observational data do not record secondary cancers, so the emulated endpoint is recurrence-free survival. The substitution is dismissed as semantic on the grounds that 13 of the trial's 176 events were secondary cancers, but the entire framework then tunes weights until the emulated recurrence-free survival matches the trial's disease-free survival, so a 7 percent endpoint difference is absorbed into the parameter that is supposed to be correcting for unobserved confounding.
problems.quote: In our observational dataset, we record recurrence and death, but not secondary cancers, which means our endpoint is recurrence-free survival (RFS).

problems.evidence: The design premise is that a trial to emulate can nearly always be found, and the framework requires the trial's published control-arm survival and covariate means as inputs before the cohort is even selected. The target trial is therefore chosen from the set of trials whose results are already known, and the eligibility, matching and weighting are all conditioned on those results. Inference proceeds as though the protocol had been fixed in advance.
problems.quote: it is almost always possible to find an existing trial to emulate

problems.evidence: A multi-institutional consortium cohort of 779 eligible patients yields an analysis cohort of 216, and the treated arm shrinks from 140 to 108, so the constraint is the scarcity of treated patients. Optimal policy trees with five nodes are then trained on those 216 patients, and the tree that assigns 186 of 216 to benefit is validated by log-rank tests on node-level subsets of an already small sample.
problems.quote: This resulted in deriving an emulated cohort of 216 patients (108 treated with surgery alone and 108 treated with surgery plus adjuvant chemotherapy)

problems.evidence: Subgroup treatment recommendations come from policy trees trained on counterfactual survival models whose cross-validated C-indices are 0.68 untreated and 0.61 treated, close to chance, while the in-sample C-index of 0.88 is what the framework relies on. The reward constraint that decides how many subgroups get recommended treatment was set at 0.78 because that was the largest value that still allowed a split, so the subgroup structure is a function of a tuning choice made to obtain splits rather than of evidence about heterogeneity.
problems.quote: This was the largest constraint we could apply while still allowing the OPT to split.

papers.title: The importance of properly specifying your target trial emulation: commentary on Mésidor et al.
papers.one_line: A letter arguing that a statin emulation reporting biologically implausible effects failed through misaligned time zero rather than residual confounding, since treatment was defined from the first three months of follow-up and early outcomes were excluded after baseline.
papers.what_was_done: The study under discussion used Quebec administrative health data to estimate the effect of statins for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in older adults and reported effects that were biologically implausible and inconsistent with prior evidence, unchanged by a range of sensitivity analyses, and presented that as a cautionary tale about target trial emulation's limits against confounding. The letter locates a different failure. Treatment was defined as persistence to statins, yes or no, among people newly prescribed statins, and that status was determined from the first three months of follow-up rather than at time zero. An exclusion criterion removed people who experienced the outcome within the first month of follow-up, again using post-baseline information to define baseline status. Both moves classify patients using information that did not exist at the moment follow-up begins, which is the standard route to immortal time bias. The letter's position is that this misalignment, not residual confounding, is the larger contributor to the implausible estimates, that eligibility and assignment must rest solely on information available at time zero, and that a design failing the alignment requirement should not carry the emulation label. It also notes that the analytic code was not shared, which leaves the diagnosis a hypothesis.

future_research.gap: Without shared code the cause of an implausible emulation result cannot be established from the publication
future_research.quote: had the authors shared their analytic code, we would have more certainty as to the potential causes of the observed results

problems.evidence: Persistence to statins was determined over the first three months after baseline and used to classify patients at baseline, and the outcome-free window used for exclusion ran one month past baseline. Both windows are design parameters that were selected without any outcome-blind rule and both use post-baseline information, and the letter's argument is that these choices, not confounding, produced effects large enough to be biologically implausible. The published sensitivity analyses varied other things and left the estimates unchanged.
problems.quote: This was not defined at time zero, but rather using the first 3 months of follow-up.

problems.evidence: The dispute is over whether an analysis carrying the emulation label is one, and the letter's remedy is to withdraw the label from designs that fail temporal alignment. That is exactly the situation where the label was doing work it cannot do: it was invoked in the original report to argue that only confounding remained, and the letter has to reconstruct the design from the published description to contest it. Nothing about the label constrained what the analysis actually did.
problems.quote: a design that does not successfully achieve this cannot reasonably be called a TTE

problems.evidence: The diagnosis of what went wrong is explicitly a hypothesis because the analytic code was not published, and the letter's authors state they cannot tell exactly how time zero and exposure were defined. A published emulation reporting implausible results therefore cannot be debugged by readers, and the correction of the record depends on the original team's cooperation rather than on inspectable artifacts.
problems.quote: We encourage all authors to share their code and/or detailed methods to encourage reproducibility and replicability

problems.evidence: Two competent groups read the same published analysis and attribute the implausible estimates to different assumptions, one to residual confounding and one to temporal misalignment, and neither can settle it from the report. A structure that separated the diagnosable assumptions, whether eligibility, assignment and time zero coincide, from the undiagnosable one, no unmeasured confounding, would have resolved this at the reporting stage; instead both are argued in prose after publication.
problems.quote: we are uncertain as to exactly how time zero (start of follow-up) and exposure were defined in this study

problems.evidence: The original study ran a range of sensitivity analyses and none altered the implausible finding, which was read as evidence that confounding was intractable. If the letter's diagnosis is right, the analyses were varying the confounding assumption while a design assumption was violated, and no combination of one-at-a-time variations could reveal that. A sensitivity program that cannot distinguish immortal time from unmeasured confounding returns stability regardless of which is failing.
problems.quote: A range of sensitivity analyses did not alter this finding.

problems.evidence: The intended protocol component is a treatment strategy assigned at baseline; what the data supplied was persistence measured over three months of follow-up, and the estimand became a contrast between groups defined by their own future behavior. That is a different quantity from the initiation strategy the target trial specifies, not a noisier measurement of it, and the resulting estimates were large enough to be biologically implausible.
problems.quote: In this study, treatment was defined as persistence to statins (yes or no) among people newly prescribed statins.

papers.title: "Real-World" Evidence, Target Trial Emulation, and Randomized Clinical Trials-Which Data Should Clinicians Rely on When Choosing Antibiotics?
papers.one_line: An invited commentary on a Danish emulation of early oral switch for gram-negative bloodstream infection rejects the inference that agreement with a randomized trial licenses substituting observational evidence, noting that more than 100 clinician-initiated antibiotic trials ran in the previous decade.
papers.what_was_done: The emulation under discussion compared early transition to oral antibiotics against a complete intravenous course in adults with uncomplicated gram-negative bloodstream infection in Denmark, concluding the strategy safe and effective on similar 90-day all-cause mortality. The randomized trial it is said to agree with used a different endpoint, a composite of death, additional antimicrobial therapy, microbiological relapse or infection-related readmission at 90 days, and reported non-inferiority. The same group's separate emulation compared 5 to 7 day against 8 to 14 day treatment durations on 90-day mortality, where three randomized trials had already reported short-course equivalence. The commentary sets against the premise that antibiotic trials are infeasible: more than 100 clinician-initiated randomized trials of antibiotic use were completed in the preceding decade, trials enrolling more than 1,000 patients per arm have recently completed, a multicontinental platform trial in Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection is running, trial networks operate across the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Europe and Asia, and one US trial embedded randomization in the electronic health record under a consent waiver. Open questions named as still requiring trials include the timing of the switch and which oral agent to use, specifically whether beta-lactams suffice against fluoroquinolones or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

future_research.gap: The switch timing and the choice of oral agent within the strategy remain undetermined
future_research.quote: further data are required to determine the ideal timing of EOS and to identify the most effective oral agents for this strategy

problems.evidence: The inference under challenge is stated in its bare form: a rigorous emulation reached the same conclusion as a trial, therefore observational data could replace trials for decisions of this type. The commentary's answer is a position rather than a theory, that observational data should be used when trials are unavailable, and no argument on either side connects the properties of the replicated question, an uncomplicated infection with a clean 90-day mortality endpoint, to the questions the extrapolation would cover.
problems.quote: can clinicians bypass the need for RCTs and simply base their decision-making on observational data?

problems.evidence: Agreement is asserted between an emulation whose outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality and a trial whose outcome was a four-part composite of death, additional antimicrobial therapy, microbiological relapse and infection-related readmission, and the trial result was non-inferiority against a margin rather than an effect estimate. No common scale, no margin and no interval is computed across the pair, so what is recorded is a concordance label between two different estimands.
problems.quote: The use of observational data should be hypothesis-generating rather than confirming the results of RCTs.

problems.evidence: Early oral switch is a single strategy label covering a choice of switch day and a choice of agent, and the open questions named are exactly which day and which drug, with beta-lactams, fluoroquinolones and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole plausibly not interchangeable. The emulation estimated an effect for the label, so its estimate averages over versions whose relative efficacy is the actual clinical question, and no procedure defines which versions belong in the class.
problems.quote: This includes investigating whether β-lactam antibiotics are adequate as oral step-down agents in treating these infections, as opposed to fluoroquinolones or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

problems.evidence: The commentary has to state explicitly that the real-world label neither adds value over trial data nor removes confounding, which is the work the label was doing in the exchange. It endorses the methods as the right choice when observational data are used and still declines to let the design name carry any weight in prescribing decisions, so the label and the assumption burden are being separated by hand in the editorial rather than by anything the study reports.
problems.quote: Applying the real-world label to observational data does not somehow make it more valuable to clinicians than data from RCTs, nor does it eliminate confounding.

problems.evidence: The recommendation on when emulation-derived evidence may drive prescribing is given as a belief, that observational data should primarily be used when trials are not available, immediately after conceding that modern causal inference still leaves confounding. No threshold distinguishes an emulation that would change practice from one that would not, so the decision rests on the reader's judgment about a class of evidence rather than on any property of the analysis in front of them.
problems.quote: It is our belief that the use of observational data to compare different antibiotic use strategies should primarily be used when data from RCTs are not available.
